XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT The P.I., of Mahadevapura Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, she got married with accused No.1 on 08.05.2008 at Guruvayurappa Temple, Kerala, in the presence of the elders, at the time of marriage as per the say of the accused No.1, the parents of the CW.1 i.e, CW.2 and 3 have given 35 Sovereign Gold ornaments, Cash of Rs.3,50,000/-, Chain, Titan Watch as dowry and they also arranged reception on 16.05.2008 at E.C.A Club Auditorium, Indiranagar.

It is further alleged that, the complainant went to M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
2 C.C.No.22242/2011 her matrimonial house at Chinnappa Building,
Chinnappanahalli, Mahadevapura along with accused No.1 and 2 and accused No.3 and 4 were also resided in the same building.

It is further contended that, the accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have forced CW.1 to take more dowry from her parental house, after giving some money from her parental house also they have subjected CW.1 to cruelty for more dowry by harassing her both physically and mentally.
It is further alleged that, on 20.08.2010 accused No.1 to 4 picked up quarrel with CW.1 and dragged her from the matrimonial house to take more dowry from her parental house.

Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1, CW.14 has registered the case against accused No.1 to 4 in P.S. Crime No.351/2010 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a), 506 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Investigating Officers/ CW.14 and 15 have investigated the matter, CW.15 after completion of the investigation has submitted final report against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offence punishable U/s 498(A) R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
produced before this court and later they were released on bail.
Accused No.2 and 3 have obtained anticipatory bail.
Upon C.C.No.22242/2011 receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offence alleged against the accused No.1 to 4 and registered the criminal case against them.
After registration of the case, copies of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to them in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused No.1 and 4 only.
They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

4. In order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4, the prosecution has examined 05 witness out of 15 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 to PW.5 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.09 and closed its side.
Thereafter, the accused No.1 to 4 were examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against them.
The accused No.1 to 4 have denied the same.
The accused No.1 examined himself as DW.1 and got marked nine documents as per Ex.D.1 to 9 and closed his side.
5. Heard both sides.

The counsel for accused has relied on the following decisions;
i) 2009 AIR SCW 6683 SC C.C.No.22242/2011 ii) (2010) 7 SCC 667 iii) (2009) 13 SCC 330 6.
Perused the materials on record.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused No.1 was married with CW.1 on 08.05.2008 and thereafter, the complainant went to her matrimonial house along with accused No.1 and 2 and accused No.3 and 4 were also residing in the same building, the accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both by physically and mentally and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused No.1 got married with CW.1 on 08.05.2008 at Guruvayuru, at that time, CW.2 and 3 have provided dowry of Rs.3,50,000/-, 35 Sovereign Gold, Watch and accused No.1 has C.C.No.22242/2011 received the same and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all has demanded more dowry from CW.1 and subjected her to cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?
4. What Order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the Negative.
 Point No.4 : As per the final order  for the following;
 REASONS  9. POINT Nos.1 to 3 :-
As these three points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repeti- tion of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has to establish that, the accused No.1 to 4 C.C.No.22242/2011 have subjected CW.1 to cruelty, harassed her both physically and mentally for the purpose of dowry.

10. In order to prove the above said allegations, the prosecution has examined CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, she deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was solemnized on 08.05.2008 at Guruvayuru, at the time of marriage, the accused No.1 was given dowry of 35 Sovereign of Gold, Chain and Titan Watch.
After marriage, accused No.1 was given a bike, the marriage expenses were borne by the parents of the complainant.

She has further deposed that, thereafter, she went to the house of the accused No.1 at Mahadevapura and for two months, the accused No.1 took proper care and thereafter, started demanding more money, accordingly, the complainant paid a sum of Rs.25,000/- and Rs.35,000/-.

CW.1 has further deposed that, accused M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
4 No.2 to 4 were demanding her golden ornaments to pledge before Muthoot Finance.
She has further deposed that, when she went to her parental house for delivery, she has paid Rs.1.35 Lacks for releasing the pledged golden ornaments.
She has further deposed that, in the month of November, when accused No.1 came to house, on that day, he assaulted CW.1.
She has further deposed that, ac- cused persons in furtherance of common intention subjected CW.1 to cruelty and thereafter, the accused have abused the C.C.No.22242/2011 parents of the complainant.
CW.1 has further deposed regard- ing filing of complaint and drawing of Mahazar.

11. The parents of the complainant i.e., CW.2 and 3 were examined as PW.2 and 3, wherein, they deposed that, the marriage of CW.1 with accused No.1 took place on 08.05.2008 and the marriage expenses were borne by CW.2.
PW.2 and 3 are further deposed that, reception was taken place on 16.05.2008.
At the time of marriage, on demand of the accused No.1, PW.2 has given 35 Sovereign Gold and 05 Sovereign gold, Wrist Watch and Honda Activa Scooty were give to Accused No.1.
After two months of marriage, on de- mand of accused persons, PW.2 and 3 have paid Rs.25,000/- and Rs.35,000/- and also given refrigerator and TV.
PW.2 and 3 have further deposed that, the accused persons were fre- quently demanding for money and assaulted CW.1, Panchay- ath were conveyed between CW.1 and accused persons.

12. The official, who apprehended accused No.4 has been examined as PW.4, wherein, he deposed that, on 28.09.2010, he along with CW.13 were deputed to apprehend accused persons, when they were doing patrolling duty appre- hended accused No.1 and 4 and produced before IO.

. The part investigation carried out by the official i.e., CW.14 was examined as PW.5, wherein, he deposed that, on receipt of complaint from CW.1, he registered the case and forwarded the FIR to the court.
14. It is pertinent to mention here that, PW.2 was reported to be dead.
Inspite of providing sufficient opportuni- ties, the prosecution has failed to examine the investigation of- ficer.

15. DEFENCE EVIDENCE AND EXHIBIT 'D' SERIES:-
The accused No.1 in order to prove his defence has examined himself as DW.1,
wherein, he deposed that, as per the request and consent of the complainant, they got married on 08.05.2008 at Guruvayuru and the marriage expenses were equally borne by the parents of the complainant and accused No.1.
He has further deposed that, whenever accused No.1 did good to his mother, CW.1 did not tolerated and by listening to the words of her mother, used to picked up quarrel.
DW.1 has further deposed that, when she went for delivery and did not came back and when enquired CW.1 contended that, she would come only if accused No.1 would be separated from his mother.

DW.1 has further deposed that, he has purchased one C.C.No.22242/2011 M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
5 Bike in the month of February 2009 in the name of CW.1 and he has paid EMI.

DW.1 has further deposed that, on 30.07.2010 from 9.30 PM, till 31.07.2010 at 7.00 PM, he was working at Devanahalli Airport, accordingly, the complainant has falsely implicated the accused No.1 in the case.
Receipts are produced and marked as Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.7.

Copy of dis- charge summary and attendance certificate were got marked as Ex.D.8 and 9.
16.
In the case on hand, it is the prosecution, who has to establish its case against the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubt.
To counter blast the defence raised by the accused No.1, PW.1 was further examined and got marked documents relating to repayment of loan towards purchase of Honda Activa Bike as Ex.P.7 to 9.

Ex.P.8 is the Form No.35, wherein, it reveals that, the agreement of higher purchase en- tered into between the Bank and the complainant with regard to bike No.KA-53-L-4863 was terminated, in other words, the loan availed was cleared.
Ex.P.9 is the Bank Statement with regard to the loan account No.144676816, wherein, loan was availed to purchase Honda Activa in the name of CW.1.

En- tries in the statement reveals that, repayment has been made vide cheques and by cash.
C.C.No.22242/2011 17.

Ex . D.1, which is the repayment receipt issued by the HDFC Bank with regard to the two wheeler loan, A/c num- ber mentioned is 14476816 dated:16.09.2009 in the name of the complainant,
wherein, an amount of Rs.2,277/- have been paid towards EMI.
Ex.D.2 to 7 are also the repayment receipts with regard to the express loan plus in the name of accused No.1 for having been paid EMI.
I have carefully examined Ex.D.2 to 7, wherein, those receipts pertains to some other loan account not with the loan account of the complainant.

Therefore, on conjoint reading of Ex.P.8 and 9, Ex.D.2 to 7, it reveals that, loan for purchase of two wheeler was availed in the name of the complainant and EMI has been paid towards repayment of loan and loan has been closed on 30.01.2010.
The only question remained is as to who has paid the EMI.
Ex.D.1 refers that, the accused has paid one month EMI, which is also admitted by CW.1 during her cross examination.
On perusal of Ex.P.9, which is the Bank Statement, as detailed above by way of cheques and cash, the EMI is has been paid.
The accused No.1 has not produced sufficient evidence in or- der to show that, he has paid entire EMI and cleared the amount.

Therefore, his defence that, he purchased the bike in the name of CW.1 and entire EMI has been a paid by him holds no water.
C.C.No.22242/2011 18.
Ex . D.8 is the Discharge Bill of the complainant, wherein, she was admitted in Chinmaya Mission Hospital on 01.12.2009 and discharged on the same day.
It also does not throw light on the defence of the accused and will not come in aid in support of the defence of the accused No.1.
Ex.D.9 is the certified copy of the Attendance register, wherein, it has been revealed that, on 30.07.2010 the accused No.1 had worked with Kingfisher Airlines Limited.

The accused No.1 sets up defence that,
on the day of incident of assault, he was working at Kingfisher Airlines from 9.30 PM to 7.AM on 31.07.2010.

No doubt, Ex.D.9 fortifies that, he was working on the said day, but he has not furnished M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
6 and adduced the evi- dence of the competent authority and also produced document showing that,
he was working from 9.30 AM on the said day till 7.00 AM on the next working day.
Therefore, the said de- fence of the plea of alibi also holds no water.
19. The other defence raised by the accused that, CW.1 submitted that, if he leaves his mother he will come back to the house also holds no water as there is no sufficient evidence in that regard.

Neverthless, as discussed in my earlier paragraphs, the prosecution, who has to establish its case be- yond reasonable doubts and accused persons are not having any burden to prove their defence.
C.C.No.22242/2011 20. ANALYSIS:-
Having gone through the ocular evidence led in by the prosecution and accused No.1,
as discussed the prosecution has to establish that for the purpose of dowry, the accused No.1 to 4 have subjected CW.1 to cruelty.

On conjoint reading of cross examination part of PW.1 and 3 and DW.1, the accused No.1 has failed to show that,
the accused No.1 and CW.1 were loving each other and after discussion with the family got arranged the marriage.

I would like to rely on relevant portions of the cross examination of PW.1, wherein, she has admitted that, she has not deposed as to the marriage has been made by Thomas Mathew and CW.1 has not filed any complaint against the said Thomas Mathew.
Cross examination of PW.1 further reveals that, she has admitted that, 35 Sovereign golden were given in order to wear by the complainant.

PW.1 has admitted that, she stayed at the matri- monial house till her 7th month of pregnancy and at that time, accused No.3 and 4 were not residing and have also not given any complaint against them for harassing her.
PW.1 has also admitted that, after getting divorce from accused No.1, he has paid Rs.6000/- per month till the year 2018.
On careful perusal of cross examination of PW.3, she has admitted that, they have not given any complaint against the accused persons.
PW.3 has admitted that, in the month of June, CW.1 was returned to the parental house and CW.1 gave birth to male child in the month of September.
PW.3 has further admitted that, since then, they have not met accused persons.
22. On perusal of the cross examination of PW.1, PW.3 and in conjoint reading of documentary evidence ad- duced by the prosecution, there are material discrepancies.
23. Cruelty for the purpose of section 498A of IPC is to be established in the context of section 498A of IPC as it may be different from other statutory provisions.
It is to be de- termined by considering the conduct of the man, weighing the gravity or seriousness of his acts and to find out as to whether the women was subjected to cruelty.
It is to be established that, the women has been subjected to cruelty continuously / persis- tently or atleast in close proximity of time of lodging the com- plaint.

M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
7 24.

In Mohammed Assang V/s State of AP, reported in 2002 SCC Crl.1765, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has C.C.No.22242/2011 dealt and held that mental or physical torture should be contin- uously practiced by the husband accused on the wife.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25. In Raja Rani V/s State, reported in AIR 2000 Supreme Court 3559, the Hon'ble Apex Court considering the case of cruelty in the context of provisions of section 498A of IPC held the court must examine that the allegations for ac- cusation must be of a very grave nature and should be proved beyond reasonable doubt.

entities.text: Raja Rani V/s State, reported in AIR 2000 Supreme Court 3559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 26. The counsel for the accused has relied on a deci- sion reported in 2009 AIR SCW 6683, Supreme Court Neelu Chopra and Another and Bharathi, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has dealt with section 406, 498A of IPC, Criminal breach of trust and cruelty and quashed the proceedings.

27. The counsel for the accused has also relied on a decision reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667 between Preethi Gupta and Another V/s State of Jharkhand and another, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, allegations to be scrutinized with great care and circumspection especially against husband's relatives, who were living in different cities.
28.

entities.text: Preethi Gupta and Another V/s State of Jharkhand and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The counsel for accused has also relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2009)
13 SCC C.C.No.22242/2011 330, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has dealt with cruelty, its proof and proximity test.
29.
I have carefully gone through the entire materials on record, the prosecution has failed to establish that, the CW.1 has been subjected to cruelty continuously / persistently by the accused persons.
No independent witnesses have been examined by the prosecution.
No sufficient evidence has been adduced by the prosecution in order to show that, the accused No.1 was given with gold jewels, cash, watch, Honda Activa Scooter.

The evidence on record is not sufficient to conclude that,
the accused No.1 to 4 have demanded more money from the complainant.
At the same time, the accused No.1 has failed to establish his defence.
There is no sufficient evidence against accused No.3 and 4 for having subjected CW.1 to cruelty as the evidence of PW.1 and PW.3 are contrary to the said ver- sions.
In the case on hand, the prosecution has failed to secure the presence of IO and led his evidence.
Non examination of IO is fatal to the case of the prosecution.
Even though, CW.1 and 3 have supported the case of the prosecution, but they are interested witnesses.
Much reliance cannot be placed on their testimonies as there are material discrepancies and contradic- tions as compared with other documentary evidence.

On over all perusal of the materials on record, the prosecution has failed to establish that, the accused No.1 to 4 have subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both physi- cally and mentally and also failed to prove that the accused No.1 to 4 have demanded dowry from the complainant.
In ab- sence of sufficient oral and documentary evidence, it cannot be concluded that, the accused persons have committed the crime as alleged.
In such circumstances, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to accused persons as the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

M.D.Pura P.S vs Priyesh on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73486567/
8
Accordingly, the Point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the "Negative".

31. Point No. 4 :- In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The Bail bonds and surety bonds of the accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force C.C.No.22242/2011 for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
